coordinateBasis: Rounded J2000/ICRS catalogue centres for a small orientation finder; not telescope pointing or photometric predictions.

targets.name: M31 · Andromeda Galaxy
targets.hint: Start in Andromeda; diffuse extended light, with a brighter core. Dark skies and a wide field help.

targets.name: M42 · Orion Nebula
targets.hint: Below Orion’s belt, in the sword. Optical detail depends on conditions and equipment.

targets.name: M45 · Pleiades
targets.hint: A broad cluster in Taurus. Binoculars offer a wider overview than high magnification.

targets.name: M13 · Hercules Cluster
targets.hint: In Hercules. Binoculars may show a patch; resolving individual stars needs suitable optics.

targets.name: M57 · Ring Nebula
targets.hint: Between the southern stars of Lyra. Small target; a telescope and finder practice are useful.

landmarks.name: Orion · Alnilam, belt centre
landmarks.hint: Middle star of Orion’s three-star belt. The nebula lies in the sword below the belt.

landmarks.name: Lyra · Vega
landmarks.hint: Bright anchor for Lyra; use the small parallelogram to work towards M57.

landmarks.name: Ursa Minor · Polaris
landmarks.hint: Northern-sky anchor near the celestial pole. Not visible from most southern latitudes.

landmarks.name: Ursa Major · Dubhe
landmarks.hint: One of the Big Dipper’s bowl stars; the Dipper is an asterism within Ursa Major.

landmarks.name: Carina · Canopus
landmarks.hint: Bright southern-sky anchor in Carina; unavailable from far northern latitudes.
